newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela says France wants bilingual U.N. chief.
newsitem.headline: Mandela says France wants bilingual U.N. chief.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela said on Sunday French President Jaques Chirac would veto any candidate for U.N. secretary-general who did not speak French, ruling out Salim Ahmed Salim of Tanzania.

"I spoke at length last night to Jacques Chirac, who insists that a candidate for the secretary-generalship of the United Nations must be fluent in both English and French, and he is not prepared to support any candidate who does not have these qualifications," Mandela told a news conference.
"He said he will veto Salim Salim if he is nominated," Mandela said.
Mandela said South Africa supported the Tanzanian, who is now secretary-general of the Organisation of African Unity.
"On merit, he is a highly capable man," he said. "We think he is the best candidate for the job."

The OAU, which threw its weight behind Egypt's Boutros Boutros-Ghali at its annual summit in Cameroon in July, threw the door open to other Africans when he set aside his candidacy last Wednesday after a November 19 U.S. veto in the Security Council blocked his path to the now traditional second term.
